question.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ where $f(x)=\frac{-7{x}^{4}+3}{2{x}^{2}-4}.$
question.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{-7{x}^{4}+3}{2{x}^{2}-4} \\  & {lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{-7{x}^{4}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{2{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{4}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(-7{x}^{2}+\frac{3}{{x}^{2}})}{(2-\frac{4}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{-7{x}^{2}+0}{2-0} \\  & =\frac{7}{2}{lim}_{x\to \infty }(-{x}^{2}) \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.
